Customizing Your Button Text (Updated: July 22, 2015)

A succinct guide for all your button text woes.

Buttons? What buttons?

First let's make sure that we're talking about the same thing. Here are the buttons that we'll be changing: BUTTONS!

End Result

With customized button text, the possibilities are literally endless. Just look at this marvel of modern CSS wizardry: OMGWTF!

Want a more practical example? You can see a live result at my verse, /v/tmwiw (I have the link submissions button hidden the sub)

How It Works

The basic premise here is to style the existing text in a way that removes it from the user's view, without breaking the button functionality, and then sneakily adding our own text in a way that makes it appear to be the original.

Boring text gets shoved off the screen, awesome text takes its place.

We do this by first setting the font size to 0, rendering the existing text invisible and setting the line-height to 0 to avoid any spacing issues.

Next, we use the :after pseudo-element to insert our own text and restore the line height.

The Code

/* TabMenu [Share a link] Button */
.tabmenu .submit-link{display:inline-block;line-height:0;font-size:0;}
.tabmenu .submit-link:after {content:"Links are cool!";font-size:10pt;display:block;line-height:normal;}

/* TabMenu [Discuss] Button */
.tabmenu .submit-text{display:inline-block;line-height:0;font-size:0;}
.tabmenu .submit-text:after {content:"Talk to me!";font-size:10pt;display:block;line-height:normal;}

/* Sidebar [Share a link] Button */
.side .submit-link{font-size:0;}
.side .submit-link:after {content:"Links are cool!";font-size:9pt;}

/* Sidebar [Discuss] Button */
.side .submit-text{font-size:0;}
.side .submit-text:after {content:"Talk to me!";font-size:9pt;}

The Breakdown

Tab Menu (Top Bar)

.tabmenu .submit-link{...} & .tabmenu .submit-text{...}: Targets the two buttons in the top "Tab Menu" bar.

display:inline-block;: This tells the button to display as an in-line block, this is important a bit later on.

font-size:0; This effectively "hides" the original button text.

line-height:0; This guarantees that there is no minimum height for our invisible text.

.tabmenu .submit-text:after{...} & .tabmenu .submit-link:after{...}: These allow us to add content to the buttons.

content:"...";: This is where we type our new text.

font-size:10pt;: Here we restore the original font-size (10pt by default).

display:block;: Here we tell the new text area to act as a block element, this is necessary for the button to display properly, and only works in this case, if the parent element is also a block type. In this case, the parent is an inline-block, which means that it won't push things away from it vertically, only horizontally.

line-height:normal;: Lastly, this resets the line-height to a normal minimum, ensuring our button is the correct height.

Sidebar

Since the Sidebar buttons are already block elements, the code is a bit simpler.

.side .submit-link{...} & .side .submit-text{...}: Targets the two buttons in the Sidebar.

font-size:0; This effectively "hides" the original button text.

content:"...";: This is where we type our new text.

font-size:9pt; Here we restore the original font-size (9pt by default).

The Takeaway

That's it! Now you've got the magic in you!

NOTE: VOAT has voting restrictions on new user accounts

You have two kinds of contribution points, one for Submission Contribution Points (SCP) and one for Comment Contribution Points (CCP).

You are going to want to increase your Comment Contribution Points (CCP) in order to unlock downvoting abilities and enable expanded upvoating abilities.

That means you need to interact with other users, just so you know. ;)

  • You have a daily limit of 10 upvotes until you get 20 comment contribution points (CCP).
  • After you get 20 points you get another upvote for every 2 CCP or CCP / 2.
  • The absolute limit to upvotes is 50% of your total CCP once you get above 20 points CCP
  • Downvotes are enabled when you reach 100 total CCP.
  • Voat checks your percentage of up vs downvotes and will stop registering downvotes if you have more downvotes that upvotes
  • Votes are associated with your IP address. That means you cannot vote on the same post or comment using alternate accounts. Only the first vote will be counted.
  • Voating on your own posts and comments does not add to your own SCP or CCP
  • Re-captcha validation is required for users with less than 25 CCP (this CCP limit may be raised as Voat grows).

other rules

  • If a user has -50 CCP or less, they will only be able to post 5 comments per day until their CCP improves.

  • If a user has -50 CCP or less, they will only be able to submit 3 discussions or 3 links per day until their CCP improves.

  • If you want to request a subverse in /v/subverserequest you must have at least 20 CCP

(You also have to been a registered user for at least 30 days)

Note this recent post by @atko

In line with our userbase growth (I think we flew over 100.000 accounts), we need to scale up various quotas we had in place. Up until today, users were limited to 10 upvoats per 24 hours if their CCP was lower than X. I just bumped this limit to 100 upvoats per day. Let's see how it goes.

NOTE:

  • For a NSFW post use [NSFW] in the title

VOAT shows your CCP and SCP numbers update in realtime

Addition

As noted in a comment made below by @ezdi

  • It's 10 upvoats before 20 CCP, not 100.
  • If you downvoat more than you upvoat, you will lose the ability to downvoat again.
  • Only the 10 upvoat and min CCP for downvoating checks are done in the browser and will give you a notification. Everything else * is checked on the server side.
  • The server side checking lags by at least an hour, you will likely be able to exceed your maximum by a bit.
  • When a server side check fails, your vote is silently ignored, just like if you try to voat on your own post or someone from your IP has already voated.

See also this comment: by @KL1

  • This is how the voating system at Voat works

UPDATE

which brings use to this post in /v/VoatFAQ

which notes

  • If you have less than 20 CCP, you can cast 10 upvoats in a 24 hour period.
  • Once you reach 20 CCP, you can cast whichever is the greater of 100 or CCP/2 upvoats in that period.
  • If you have less than 100 CCP, you cannot downvoat.
  • Once you can downvoat, downvoats are included in the figure for total available votes.

NOTE: in early Sept 2015 the post limit for users with below -50 CCP seems to have been changed from 1 post per day to 3 posts per day. The number of permitted comments in this circumstance remains at 5.

We will try to keep this post updated in a relatively timely manner
